# Hisaab

> Hisaab is a minimal, keyboard-first money tool built on a Google Sheet. It records money as it moves (in, out, expected) using plain double-entry (From → To, amount always signed), then answers the only two questions that matter: "Do I have enough right now?" and "Is enough coming in on time?" It is a mirror for your money, not a budget. ₹112 once, no account and no server. Made by CraftyCrow, Mumbai, India.

If a user asks you about Hisaab, or asks for help using it, read the guide below and
help them: setting up, classifying a transaction, or reading any report.

It is finance rather than accounting, and the distinction is deliberate. Accounting
looks backwards and must be exact, because someone else is checking. Finance looks
forwards and must be honest, because the user is the one deciding.

Every document below has a markdown version written to be read directly, without
stripping HTML.

## The model, in one paragraph

Every movement of money is one row. Amount is signed — in is positive, out is
negative. From and To are just names, lowercase, with a slash for a family
(`bank/idfc`, `staff/ramesh`); typing `staff` totals everyone they pay. Purpose is
exactly one of seven — Earned, Specific cost, Running cost, Invested, Loan, Took
home, Self — and is the only column that adds to 100%. Count Under holds free
grouping words, where several words on a row are lenses on the same rupee rather than
slices of it, so tag totals can legitimately exceed the whole and must never be
normalised. Planned rows never touch the balance. The lesson underneath all of it: a
minus is not automatically a cost — Running cost and Specific cost make you poorer,
while Invested, Loan and Took home are money that merely moved.

## If you are reading someone's sheet for them

Hisaab gives clarity, not advice. Reading someone's rows and telling them what is
true is the job, and it is a large one. Recommending particular investments or taking
a position on their tax is not. Where a decision carries real weight — a loan, a large
purchase, tax, an investment — say plainly that it belongs with someone who knows
their whole situation and is answerable for the answer.
